newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest power eases as milder temps take over.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest power eases as milder temps take over.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the midwestern U.S. eased Monday as milder temperatures took over much of the region, industry sources said.

Temperatures through much of the Mid-West were expected to be normal and above normal through to Wednesday, with some cooling expected later in the week and temperatures four to eight degrees Fahrenheit below normal by Friday.
A return to more normal temperatures from last week's frigid levels helped drop power demand and pushed prices lower.
Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), Tuesday peak, non-firm power prices were discussed at $17.00-19.00 from $18.00-20.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) late last week, the brokers and marketers said.
Off-peak Tuesday non-firm MAPP power eased to $11.00-12.00 from $12.00-14.00 late last week, the sources said.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), peak, non-firm power prices for Tuesday were talked at $16.00-18.00 from $18.00-20.00 late last week.
MAIN off peak next day power was also said to be talked at $11.00-12.00 from $12.00-14.00 per MWh.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Tuesday moved lower to $15.00-17.00 from $24.00-26.00 last week, although some $19.00 next-day power was said to have been talked in the north of the region on Monday.
ECAR electricity prices for off-peak, non-firm delivery were notionally assessed steady at $13.00-15.00 per MWh.
February ECAR was said to have eased to $22.50-23.00 from $23.50-24.00 late last week.

In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) peak, non-firm power prices for Tuesday delivery were talked at 16.00-18.00 through the entire region from discussion at $20.00-22.00 late last week, the sources said.
Off-peak next day prices throughout SPP were pegged at $12.00-13.00 from $13.00-15.00 last week.
February SPP was said to have eased to $22.50-23.00 from $23.00-24.00 per MWh, the sources said.
